#Part B Conditional Statements

```{r}
temp <- 33

} else {
  print("Not hot")
}
```

#Question 2

#Question 5
```{r}
#'if' checks a single TRUE/FALSE condition to control code flow (like running blocks of code or branches), while 'ifelse()' is vectorized and evaluates a condition element by element across a whole vector to return matching values. I pick 'if' for single conditions and branching logic and choose 'ifelse()' when transforming or labeling every item in a vector.
```



#Question 6
```{r}
#a. 
file_path <- "students_grades.csv"
grades <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```
```{r}
#b.
if (file.exists(file_path)) {
  grades <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  message("File imported successfully.")
} else {
  stop("Error: students_grades.csv was not found in the working directory.")
}
```
```{r}
#c.
head(grades, 6)                  # first 6 rows
dim(grades)                       # number of rows and columns
str(grades)                       # column names and data types
summary(grades)                   # basic statistics per column
colSums(is.na(grades))            # number of missing values per column
```
```{r}
#d. 
nrow(grades)                      # 1. Number of rows
ncol(grades)                      # 1. Number of columns
colSums(is.na(grades))            # 2. Which column(s) have NA and how many
class(grades$Section)             # 3. Data type of Section
range(grades$Attendance, na.rm = TRUE) # 4. Lowest and highest Attendance values
```
```{r}
#e.
nrow(grades) == 15
ncol(grades) == 7
sum(is.na(grades)) == 1
```
```{r}
#f1
grades$FinalGrade <- 0.30 * grades$Quiz + 0.30 * grades$Midterm + 0.40 * grades$Final
```
```{r}
#f2
grades$Result <- ifelse(
  is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
  NA,
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Passed", "Failed")
)
```
```{r}
#f3
grades$Remarks <- ifelse(
  is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
  NA,
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
    ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
        ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair", "Needs Improvement")
      )
    )
  )
)
```
```{r}
#f4
grades$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(grades$Attendance < 80, "At Risk", "OK")
```
```{r}
#f5
grades$Honors <- ifelse(
  !is.na(grades$FinalGrade) & grades$FinalGrade >= 90 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
  "Yes",
  "No"
)
```
```{r}
#f6
grades$Remarks_loop <- NA_character_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(grades))) {
  fg <- grades$FinalGrade[i]
  if (is.na(fg)) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- NA_character_
  } else if (fg >= 90) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Excellent"
  } else if (fg >= 85) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Very Good"
  } else if (fg >= 80) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Good"
  } else if (fg >= 75) {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Fair"
  } else {
    grades$Remarks_loop[i] <- "Needs Improvement"
  }
}
```
```{r}
#f7
# in R, a single if() expects a single TRUE/FALSE scalar, not a vector of length 15
# newer R versions give a warning or error about the condition having length > 1 (and in older R versions it only checked the first element while warning)
# the loop avoids this because grades$FinalGrade[i] passes one scalar value at a time into if()
```
```{r}
#f8
table(grades$Result, useNA = "ifany")
table(grades$AttendanceFlag, useNA = "ifany")
table(grades$Honors, useNA = "ifany")
```
```{r}
#f9
ncol(grades)
names(grades)
```

#Part Exporting Results
#Question 7
```{r}
#a. 
write.csv(grades, "full_processed_grades.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
```{r}
#b.
at_risk <- grades[!is.na(grades$AttendanceFlag) & grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]
if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("No at-risk students found; at_risk_students.csv was not written.")
}
```
```{r}
#c.
honors_rows <- !is.na(grades$Honors) & grades$Honors == "Yes"
honors <- grades[honors_rows, c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance")]

if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("No honors candidates found; honors_list.csv was not written.")
}
```
```{r}
#d.
full_check <- read.csv("full_processed_grades.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
nrow(full_check) == nrow(grades)
ncol(full_check) == ncol(grades)
all.equal(full_check, grades, check.attributes = FALSE)

if (file.exists("at_risk_students.csv")) {
  at_risk_check <- read.csv("at_risk_students.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  print(at_risk_check)
  nrow(at_risk_check) == nrow(at_risk)
}

if (file.exists("honors_list.csv")) {
  honors_check <- read.csv("honors_list.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  print(honors_check)
  nrow(honors_check) == nrow(honors)
}
```






#Question 8
```{r}
#8.1
# by default, write.csv() writes NA values as blank/empty fields in the CSV file (e.g., two commas like ,,),
# and when read back into R with read.csv(), those empty fields are parsed back as NA.
```
```{r}
#8.2
write.csv(grades, "students_grades_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(grades, "temp_compare.csv") # row.names = TRUE is the default

readLines("students_grades_processed.csv", n = 3)
readLines("temp_compare.csv", n = 3)

temp_check <- read.csv("temp_compare.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ncol(temp_check)

unlink("temp_compare.csv")
```



#Question 9
```{r}
#a.
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(
  is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
  "Pending",
  ifelse(
    !is.na(grades$Attendance) & grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
    "Full",
    ifelse(
      !is.na(grades$Attendance) & grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
      "Partial",
      "None"
    )
  )
)
```
```{r}
#b.
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(
  is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
  "Pending",
  ifelse(
    !is.na(grades$Attendance) & grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
    "Full",
    ifelse(
      !is.na(grades$Attendance) & grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
      "Partial",
      "None"
    )
  )
)
```
```{r}
#c.
scholarship_candidates <- grades[grades$Scholarship %in% c("Full", "Partial"), ]
```
```{r}
#d.
if (nrow(scholarship_candidates) > 0) {
  write.csv(scholarship_candidates, "scholarship_candidates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  message("Exported scholarship_candidates.csv successfully.")
} else {
  message("No scholarship candidates found; scholarship_candidates.csv was not written.")
}
```
```{r}
#e.
table(grades$Scholarship, useNA = "ifany")
```


#Question 10
```{r}
#1.
# checking is.na() first prevents missing grades from propagating NA or causing unexpected comparisons before thresholds are tested.
# it lets us explicitly handle or label missing values cleanly instead of leaving them unaddressed.
```
```{r}
#2.
# placing Failed before Incomplete could cause students with missing scores or grades below the cutoff to be labeled "Failed" instead of "Incomplete".
# because conditional chains evaluate in order, the earlier matching condition wins and skips the later Incomplete check.
```
```{r}
#3.
# ifelse() is better when transforming or labeling every element of a vector or column at once.
# if else is better for single TRUE/FALSE conditions that control code flow or choose between execution branches.
```
```{r}
#4.
# reading an exported CSV back into R verifies that the file was written without errors, missing rows orcolumns, or unwanted extra columns like row numbers.
# it also confirms that data types and missing values survived the export and import round trip as expected.
```
